The solution contains 0.02 M stoichiometric Ca-EDTA complex, which dissociates as follows:

\[
\text{CaY}^{2-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{Y}^{4-}
\]

Given the formation constant \(K_{\text{Ca-EDTA}} = 5 \times 10^{10}\), the dissociation constant is \(K_d = 1/K_{\text{Ca-EDTA}} = 2 \times 10^{-11}\). Let \(x\) be the equilibrium concentration of \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\). Then:

\[
K_d = \frac{[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{Y}^{4-}]}{[\text{CaY}^{2-}]} = \frac{x^2}{0.02 - x} \approx \frac{x^2}{0.02}
\]

Solving for \(x\):

\[
x^2 = K_d \times 0.02 = 2 \times 10^{-11} \times 0.02 = 4 \times 10^{-13}
\]
\[
x = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-13}} = 2 \times 10^{-6.5} \approx 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{M}
\]

The approximation \(x \ll 0.02\) is valid, so the concentration of calcium ions is \(6.3 \times 10^{-7}\) M.

Answer: D
